label: Delimiter step when first token to recall is u/q/t/2/p/g/z/j/e/1/k/3; also early i/m inputs
explanation: Mainly a delimiter-step unit: 80% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (active on 42.5% of delimiters, 8.5x lift), and the top activations (~0.95 of max) are all there. Whether it fires at <DEL> depends on which original token comes first (the first one to be output). It fires more for u, q, t, 2, p, g, z, j, e, 1, k, 3 (79% precision at <DEL> for this set, versus 18% for other first tokens). A secondary mode (~12% of mass) is on original-phase inputs i or m near the start of the sequence (t <= 3), usually weak. There is a small tail on the first copy step (recall_idx 1, ~6% of mass). It is almost silent later in the copy phase and on most other original inputs. The token set is a coarse gate: the first-token dependence is graded rather than all-or-none, and L has a weak effect (higher rate for short sequences). Dev F1 0.67, mass recall 0.80.
